key_insight: Learning local charge densities and using stochastic Kohn–Sham propagation enables global electronic-property calculations at million-atom scale without target-system self-consistent iterations or explicit diagonalization.
engineering_relevance: The framework connects atomic structure to electronic, optical and transport properties at scales relevant to materials and devices without separate models for each property.
method: Predict real-space charge density from local atomic environments.
Construct Kohn–Sham Hamiltonians from predicted densities and evaluate properties through stochastic propagation.
Use hierarchical blocking for dense-grid inference within limited GPU memory.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports density-of-states calculations for one million silicon atoms and optical and transport calculations for systems exceeding 100,000 atoms.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify prediction errors or stochastic convergence, leaving accuracy and sampling requirements important to assess.
paper_title: From local learning to global electronic properties in large-scale systems
